subject: math
title: JC H2 functions and graphs: transformations, reciprocal functions, asymptote behaviour
objectives: Describe stretches and translations of y = f(x), for changes both outside and inside the brackets
Define the key vocabulary of functions and graphs: function, transformation, stretch, translation, reciprocal function and asymptote
Sketch a reciprocal function from its asymptotes and use the root check for shifts inside the brackets

definitions.meaning: A rule that assigns exactly one output to each input: f(x) names the output of the rule f at the input x, and the graph of y = f(x) plots every input against its output.
A change to the equation of a graph that moves or resizes it in a predictable way: changes outside f act vertically, and changes inside f act horizontally and in the opposite direction to the sign.
A transformation that scales distances from an axis by a fixed factor: y = a·f(x) stretches heights by a factor of a, while y = f(bx) squeezes widths by a factor of b.
A transformation that shifts the whole graph without changing its shape: + d outside f lifts the graph by d, while + c inside the brackets shifts it left by c.
A function built from one divided by an expression, such as y = 1/x: its graph comes in separate branches divided by its vertical asymptote.
A line that a curve approaches ever more closely but never touches: y = 1/x has the vertical asymptote x = 0 and the horizontal asymptote y = 0.

mechanismSteps: y = a·f(x) + d: stretch the height, then lift the graph: multiplying by a stretches every y-coordinate by a factor of a, and adding d lifts the whole graph by d.
y = f(bx + c): read it as f(b(x + c/b)): factor out b so the shift c/b and the squeeze by b can each be read honestly.

Reciprocal functions: the asymptotes run the show: as x grows the curve flattens onto the horizontal asymptote, and as x approaches the vertical asymptote the curve shoots up it and the sign flips across it.
The +c trap: inside the brackets means shift LEFT: f(x + 3) is zero where x = -3, to the left of the original root, so the whole graph sits 3 units further left.
workedExample: Take y = f(x + 3). Its root is where the inside of the brackets is zero: x + 3 = 0 gives x = -3. The original graph had its root at x = 0, and -3 is 3 units to the left of 0, so drawing f(x + 3) means taking the whole graph of f(x) and shifting it 3 units to the left - the root check settles the direction every time.

trap.misconception: f(x + 3) shifts the graph 3 units to the right.
trap.explanation: Plus looks like a move to the right, but the shift undoes the change to x. Inside the brackets means shift LEFT: f(x + 3) is zero where x = -3, to the left of the original.
